title: An Unfinished Conversation
content:
Siddu looked at Sneha for a moment before continuing.

"The moment our eyes met, neither of us knew what to say."

A faint smile appeared on his face.

"After a few seconds, Shreya slowly walked toward one of the benches near the window and quietly sat down."

She looked at me and gently said,

"Sit."

The entire classroom was silent.

Every other student had already left.

Only the two of us remained.

I walked over and sat beside her.

For a moment...

I forgot everything around me.

The empty classroom...

The ticking clock...

The voices from outside...

None of them mattered anymore.

After three long months, she was finally sitting beside me.

I couldn't stop looking at her.

Her eyes looked tired, yet they still carried the same warmth that had made me fall for her.

For a while, neither of us spoke.

Finally, I broke the silence.

"Why didn't you come to college for so long?"

Shreya lowered her eyes.

After a brief pause, she softly replied,

"I'm... not in the mood to explain that right now."

There was a sadness in her voice that I had never heard before.

I wanted answers.

But I didn't want to make her relive something painful.

So, I smiled gently and changed the topic.

"Then tell me something else."

She looked at me.

"Why were you shifted to another section?"

A helpless smile appeared on her face.

"My attendance was too low."

She paused before continuing.

"The principal demoted me to another section."

The moment I heard those words, anger rushed through me.

How could someone be demoted just because of attendance?

For a second, I wanted to march straight to the principal's office and argue with him.

But I knew there was nothing I could do.

Another emotion quickly replaced my anger.

If she had been struggling all these months because of attendance, then what had she been going through?

Perhaps there was much more to her disappearance than I had imagined.

I forced myself to calm down.

Then...

Kiran's words echoed inside my mind once again.

"She's betraying you."

My heart resisted.

Don't ask.

But my mind wouldn't stay quiet.

After gathering all my courage, I looked at Shreya and slowly asked,

"Shreya..."

She looked at me.

"Do you know someone named Karthik?"

The moment those words left my mouth—

The classroom door slammed open.

The sudden sound echoed through the empty room.

Standing at the entrance was Satish sir.

He stood frozen for a second.

His eyes moved from me...

to Shreya...

and then back to me.

A slow smile appeared on his face.

Not a smile of happiness.

A smile of revenge.

I immediately understood.

He hadn't forgotten what had happened that morning.

Without giving either of us a chance to explain, he walked straight toward us.

"Come with me."

He grabbed my arm firmly and pulled me out of the classroom, leaving Shreya behind.

I looked back one last time.

She stood there helplessly, unable to do anything.

Within minutes...

I found myself standing outside the principal's office once again.

This time...

The principal wasn't smiling.

The moment Satish sir began explaining what had happened, the principal's face grew darker with every passing second.

Before he could say anything further, I stepped forward.

"Sir, please listen to me."

He looked at me sternly.

"Sir, she's my friend. She returned to college after a long time. I was only talking to her when Satish sir came and brought me here."

I took another step forward.

"Please believe me, sir. We're just friends."

But the principal wasn't willing to listen.

His patience had already run out.

Without another word, he called my parents and informed them about everything that had happened.

Then he looked straight into my eyes.

His voice was cold.

"From today onward, if I ever see you talking to Shreya again..."

He paused.

"You will be suspended."

For a moment...

Anger burned inside me.

I wanted to argue.

I wanted to tell him how unfair he was being.

But I knew that losing my temper would only make things worse.

Taking a deep breath, I spoke as calmly as I could.

"Sir... she's my friend. How can I pretend she doesn't exist?"

The principal slammed his hand against the table.

"That's not my concern!"

His voice echoed through the room.

"If I see you with Shreya again, you will be suspended immediately."

Silence filled the office.

Realizing there was nothing more I could say...

I walked out without saying another word.

The corridor felt longer than ever before.

For the second time that day, fate had separated me from Shreya.

And deep inside...

I had a feeling that this wouldn't be the last obstacle standing between us.
